title: Count stock calls without changing what callers see

blocks.text: The shop's stock service wants a dashboard: how many stock calls succeed and how many fail. The warehouse store `MapStock` is one implementation of `Stock`; the checkout uses another, and the tests use fakes. `MeteredStock` wraps any of them and is itself a `Stock`, so the code that calls the stock doesn't change. The dashboard reads `succeeded()` and `failed()` while checkout threads are calling.
The counters are in place. Finish `MeteredStock.level` and `MeteredStock.set` in `src/main/java/practice/Stocks.java`.

When you're done, a call through `MeteredStock` behaves exactly as a call to the stock it wraps: same answer, same exception. Every call is counted once, as a success if it returned and as a failure if it threw. Callers already catch `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative count, and some catch the exceptions their own store throws. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: every call reaches the wrapped stock with its arguments, returns its answer, and is counted as a success
calls made from several threads at once are all counted
a call that throws is counted as a failure and not as a success
a caller gets the very exception the wrapped stock threw, not another one

origin.section: One Metrics Decorator Serves Every Implementation, and Its Own Counters Must Be Thread-Safe

concepts: A decorator implements the interface it wraps and passes each call on, so one class adds metrics to every implementation while callers see the same answers and exceptions.
